knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The excluded and recorded substrate condition is shown, and levelling is offered as a separate approved variation. Accepting blame or refusing to discuss the issue does not follow the record.
Dated photographs and the recorded condition before tiling separate setting defects from substrate defects. The substrate looking sound is not a record.
The ACCC page states that the basic rights cannot be taken away by a business's own statements. Whether a particular exclusion is effective is not settled by this lesson, so advice is needed.

practicalCriteria: Given a simulated tiling job with a substrate exclusion, writes a quote that states the scope, the substrate preparation, the materials and the exclusion in writing.
Photographs a simulated substrate with the consent of the simulated client, and records the condition before any tiling is shown on the sample.
Writes a finish standard that can be measured with a straight edge over a stated length, and states how it is measured at handover.
Prices and prepares a written variation for a simulated extra levelling area, and records that it is not performed until approved.
passRule: All four practical criteria met on the simulated job, with the quote and records complete. Observed by an assessor. A knowledge check result is not a practical pass.
evidenceRequired: Signed tiling quote with scope and exclusions
Substrate condition record with dated photographs
Licence position check record for the state and job value
stopWorkCriteria: Tiling starts with no substrate record
A variation is performed without written approval
Waterproofing or structural work is quoted without the scope or authority to do it
